ψυχή.long: (a) the vital breath, breath of life, (b) the human soul, (c) the soul as the seat of affections and will, (d) the self, (e) a human person, an individual.
ψυχή.sd: breath, i.e. (by implication) spirit, abstractly or concretely (the animal sentient principle only; thus distinguished on the one hand from G4151 (πνεῦμα), which is the rational and immortal soul; and on the other from G2222 (ζωή), which is mere vitality, even of plants: these terms thus exactly correspond respectively to the Hebrew H05315, H07307 and H02416)
ψυχή.kj: heart (+ -ily), life, mind, soul, + us, + you
ψυχή.as:
ψυχή, -ῆς, ἡ,
[in LXX very freq. for נֶפֶשׁ, sometimes for לֵבַב ,לֵב, etc. ;]
1.breath (Lat. anima), breath of life, life (Hom., al.; in Arist., of the vital principle): Mt 6:25, Mk 3:410:45, Lk 12:22, Jo 10:11, Ac 20:10, 24, II Co 1:23, Phl 2:30, I Th 2:8, al.
2.the soul,
(a) as the seat of the will, desires and affections: Mt 26:38, Mk 12:30(LXX)14:34, Lk 1:46, Jo 10:24, Ac 14:2, Phl 1:27, al.; ἐκ ψυχῆς, from the heart, heartily: Eph 6:6, Col 3:23;
(b) as a periphrasis for person or self (freq. in translation from Semitic originals, v. M, Pr., 87; Robinson, Gospels, 113 ff.; but also freq. in cl., v. LS, s.v. II, 2; Edwards, Lex., App. A.): Mt 11:29, Mk 8:36, Ac 2:41, Ro 2:9, I Pe 3:20, al.; πᾶσα ψ., Ac 2:433:23 (LXX), Ro 13:1; ψ. ζῶσα (ζωῆς), I Co 15:45, Re 16:3;
(c) as the object of divine grace and eternal salvation: He 13:17, Ja 1:215:20, I Pe 1:9, 222:114:19, III Jo 2.
SYN.: v.s. νοῦς, πνεῦμα, ψυχικός, and cf. ICC on I Th 5:23, Lft., Notes, 88 f.

ψεύδομαι.sd: to utter an untruth or attempt to deceive by falsehood
ψεύδομαι.der: middle voice of an apparently primary verb;

ψευδοπροφήτης.long: a false prophet; one who in God's name teaches what is false.
ψευδοπροφήτης.sd: a spurious prophet, i.e. pretended foreteller or religious impostor
ψευδοπροφήτης.as:
† ψευδο-προφήτης, -ου, ὁ
[in LXX: Za 13:2, Je 9 (6:13, al.) (נָבִיא)* ;]
a false prophet (= cl. ψευδόμαντις): Mt 7:1524:11, 24, Mk 13:22 (v. Swete, in l.), Lk 6:26, Ac 13:6, II Pe 2:1, I Jo 4:1, Re 16:1319:2020:10 †

ψυχρός.as:
ψυχρός, -ά, -όν
(< ψύχω), [in LXX: Pr 25:25 (קַר), Si 43:20, IV Mac 11:26 * ;]
cold: sc. ὕδωρ (cf. Theogn., 263; Hdt., ii, 37), Mt 10:42; metaph., of indifferent persons, Re 3:15, 16 †

ψευδομαρτυρέω.long: I testify falsely, bear false witness.
ψευδομαρτυρέω.sd: to be an untrue testifier, i.e. offer falsehood in evidence
ψευδομαρτυρέω.as:
ψευδο-μαρτυρέω, -ῶ
[in LXX: Ex 20:16, De 5:20 (17) (ענה), Da TH Su61 AB2R (v. ψευδομάρτυς) * ;]
to bear false witness: Mt 19:18, Mk 10:19, Lk 18:20(LXX); seq. κατά, c. gen. pers., Mk 14:56, 57 (Xen., Plat., al.).†

ψύχομαι.long: I cool, pass: I grow cold.
ψύχομαι.sd: to breathe (voluntarily but gently, thus differing on the one hand from G4154 (πνέω), which denotes properly a forcible respiration; and on the other from the base of G109 (ἀήρ), which refers properly to an inanimate breeze), i.e. (by implication, of reduction of temperature by evaporation) to chill (figuratively)
ψύχομαι.as:
ψύχω
[in LXX for קוּר, שׁטח ;]
to breathe, blow; hence, to make cool. Pass., to grow cool: metaph., Mt 24:12.†

ψευδόχριστος.as:
*† ψευδό-χριστος, -ου ὁ
a false Christ or Messiah, "a pretender to the Messianic office" (Swete, Mk., 309; cf. also Tr., Syn., § xxx): Mt 24:24, Mk 13:22 (cf. ἀντίχριστος).†

ψευδόμαρτυς.sd: a spurious witness, i.e. bearer of untrue testimony
ψευδόμαρτυς.der: from G5571 (ψευδής) and a kindred form of G3144 (μάρτυς);
ψευδόμαρτυς.as:
**† ψευδο-μάρτυς, -υρος, ὁ
[in LXX: Da LXX Su 60, TH ib. 61 Bl * ;]
a false witness: Mt 26:60; c. gen. obj. (v. WM, § 30, 1a), I Co 15:15.†

ψώχω.sd: to triturate, i.e. (by analogy) to rub out (kernels from husks with the fingers or hand)
ψώχω.der: prolongation from the same base as G5567 (ψάλλω);
ψώχω.as:
† ψώχω
(< ψώω, collat. form of ψάω, to rub)
to rub: Lk 6:1.†

ψηφίζω.sd: to use pebbles in enumeration, i.e. (generally) to compute
ψηφίζω.as:
ψηφίζω
(< ψῆφος), [in LXX: III Ki 3:88:5 A (ספר ni..) * ;]
to count (prop., with pebbles), reckon, calculate: τ. δαπάνην, Lk 14:28; τ. ἀριθμόν (i.e. calculate the number's meaning), Re 13:18 (in cl. chiefly mid., to vote by casting a pebble; cf. συγ-κατα-, συμ-φηφίζω).†

ψαλμός.long: a psalm, song of praise, the Hebrew book of Psalms.
ψαλμός.sd: a set piece of music, i.e. a sacred ode (accompanied with the voice, harp or other instrument; a "psalm"); collectively, the book of the Psalms
ψαλμός.as:
ψαλμός, -οῦ, ὁ
(< ψάλλω), [in LXX chiefly for מִזְמוֹר ;]
1.a striking, twitching with the fingers (Eur., al.), hence, a striking of musical strings (Æsch., al.), and hence in later writers,
2.a sacred song sung to musical accompaniment, a psalm (LXX): I Co 14:26, Eph 5:19, Col 3:16; of OT psalms, Lk 24:44, Ac 13:33; βίβλος ψαλμῶν, Lk 20:42, Ac 1:20.†
SYN.: v.s. ὕμνος

ψηλαφάω.g: I feel, touch, handle, grope for
ψηλαφάω.long: I feel, touch, handle; I feel after, grope for.
ψηλαφάω.sd: to manipulate, i.e. verify by contact; figuratively, to search for
ψηλαφάω.der: from the base of G5567 (ψάλλω) (compare G5586 (ψῆφος));
ψηλαφάω.as:
ψηλαφάω, -ῶ
(< ψάω, to touch), [in LXX for מוּשׁ, משׁשׁ pi., etc. ;]
1.to feel or grope about; c. acc, to feel about for, search after: metaph., of seeking God, Ac 17:27.
2.to feel, touch, handle: c. acc. pers., Lk 24:39, I Jo 1:1; προσεληλύθατε ψηλαφωμένῳ (ὄρει ?), He 12:18 (R, txt., a mount that might be touched; mg., a palpable and kindled fire; v. Westc., in l.).†

ψεῦδος.long: a lie, falsehood, untruth; false religion.
ψεῦδος.as:
ψεῦδος, -εος (-ους), τό
[in LXX chiefly for שֶׁקֶר, also for כַּחַשׁ, כָּזָב ;]
a falsehood, untruth, lie: Re 14:15; opp. to ἡ ἀλήθεια, Jo 8:44, Ro 1:25, Eph 4:25, II Th 2:11, I Jo 2:21; to τὸ ἀληθές, ib. 27; ποιεῖν ψ., Re 21:2722:15; ἐν πάσῃ δυνάμει κ. σημείοις κ. τέρασιν ψεύδους (gen. qual., v. M, Th., 104; and on the meaning and construction, v. also ICC, in l.), II Th 2:9.†

ψεύστης.as:
ψεύστης, -ου, ὁ
(< ψεύδω), [in LXX: Ps 115:2 ( 116:11) (כֹּזֵב), Pr 19:22 Aא2 (כָּזָב), Si 15:825:2 * ;]
a liar: Jo 8:44, 55, Ro 3:4, I Ti 1:10, Tit 1:12, I Jo 1:102:4, 224:205:10 .†

ψωμίον.sd: a crumb or morsel (as if rubbed off), i.e. a mouthful
ψωμίον.der: diminutive from a derivative of the base of G5597 (ψώχω);
ψωμίον.as:
† ψωμίον, -ου, τό
dimin. of ψωμός, a fragment, morsel: Jo 13:26, 27, 30.†

ψῦχος.as:
ψύχος (LT, ψῦ-, as in cl.), -εος (-ους), τό
(< ψύχω), [in LXX: Ge 8:22 (קֹר), Jb 37:9, Ps 147:6 (17) (קָרָה), Za 14:6, Da LXX TH 3:67,69 * ;]
cold: Jo 18:18, Ac 28:2, II Co 11:27.†

ψευδής.as:
ψευδής, -ές
(< ψεύδομαι), [in LXX for שֶׁקֶר, שָׁוְא, כָּזָב; etc. ;]
lying, false, untrue (of persons and things): Re 2:2; μάρτυρες, Ac 6:13; as subst., ὁ ψ., a liar: Re 21:8.†

ψῆφος.long: (a) a pebble, small stone, (b) hence, from their use in voting: a vote.
ψῆφος.sd: a pebble (as worn smooth by handling), i.e. (by implication, of use as a counter or ballot) a verdict (of acquittal) or ticket (of admission); a vote
ψῆφος.as:
ψῆφος, -ου, ἡ
(< ψάω, to rub) [in LXX: Ex 4:25 (צֹר), La 3:16 (חָצָץ), Ec 7:26 (25) (חֶשְׁבּוֺך), IV Ki 12:4 (5) A, Si 18:10, IV Mac 15:26 * ;]
1.a small smooth stone, a pebble: ψ. λευκή (for suggestions as to the meaning, v. Swete, in l.), Re 2:17.
2. From the use of pebbles in voting, a vote: Ac 26:10.†

ψιθυριστής.as:
* ψιθυριστής, -οῦ, ὁ
(v. supr.),
a whisperer (as epithet of Hermes, Dem., 1358, 6): in bad sense, Ro 1:30.†
Syn.: καταλάλος, q.v

ψεῦσμα.as:
** ψεῦσμα, -τος, τό
(< ψεύδω), [in Aq., Th.: Jb 34:6, Pr 23:3; in Sm.: Jb 13:4, al. ;]
a lie, falsehood: Ro 3:7 (Plat., Plut. al.).†

ψωμίζω.sd: to supply with bits, i.e. (generally) to nourish
ψωμίζω.as:
ψωμίζω
(< ψωμός, a morsel), [in LXX chiefly for אכל hi. ;]
to feed with morsels (as children or the sick; Hippocr.), hence, generally, in late writers, to feed, nourish: c. acc. pers., Ro 12:20(LXX); c. acc rei, to give out for food, I Co 13:3 (cf. WM, § 32, 4an; for dupl. acc., cf. Nu 11:4, Si 15:3, al.).†

ψάλλω.long: I sing, sing psalms; earlier: I play on a stringed instrument.
ψάλλω.sd: compare G5597 (ψώχω)); to twitch or twang, i.e. to play on a stringed instrument (celebrate the divine worship with music and accompanying odes)
ψάλλω.der: probably strengthened from (to rub or touch the surface;
ψάλλω.as:
ψάλλω
[in LXX chiefly for זמר pi. (Jg 5:3, Ps 7:17, al.), also for נגן pi. (I Ki 16:16ff., al.) ;]
1.to pull, twitch, twang (as a bowstring, etc.; Æsch., Eur., al.), hence,
2. absol.,
(a)to play a stringed instrument with the fingers (Hdt., Plat., al.);
(b) later, to sing to a harp, sing psalms (LXX); in NT, to sing a hymn, sing praise: Ja 5:13; c. dat. pers., Ro 15:9(LXX), Eph 5:19; dat. instr., I Co 14:15.†

ψυχικός.sd: sensitive, i.e. animate (in distinction on the one hand from G4152 (πνευματικός), which is the higher or renovated nature; and on the other from G5446 (φυσικός), which is the lower or bestial nature)
ψυχικός.as:
** ψυχικός, -ή, -όν
(< ψυχή) [in LXX: IV Mac 1:32 * ;]
of theψυχή (as the lower part of the immaterial in man), EV, natural: opp. to πνευματικός, I Co 2:1415:44, 46; πνεῦμα μὴ ἔχοντες (EV, sensual; R, mg., natural or animal; better perhaps, of the mind; v. infr.), Ju 19; with ἐπίγειος, δαιμονιώδης, opp. to ἄνωθεν κατερχομένη (σοψία), of the mind (Hort, in l.), Ja 3:15†

ψευδαπόστολος.sd: a spurious apostle, i.e. pretended pracher
ψευδαπόστολος.as:
*† ψευδ-απόστολος, -ου, ὁ
a false apostle: II Co 11:13.†

ψευδάδελφος.sd: a spurious brother, i.e. pretended associate
ψευδάδελφος.as:
*† ψευδ-άδελφος, -ου, ὁ
a false brother: of professing Christians, II Co 11:26, Ga 2:4.†

ψιθυρισμός.sd: by implication, a slander; probably akin to G5574 (ψεύδομαι)); whispering, i.e. secret detraction
ψιθυρισμός.as:
† ψιθυρισμός, -οῦ, ὁ
(< ψιθυρίζω, to whisper), [in LXX: Ec 10:11 (לַחַשׁ) * ;]
a whispering;
(a) of secret slander, II Co 12:20 (Plut.);
(b) of a murmured enchantment, Ec, l.c.†

ψευδολόγος.sd: mendacious, i.e. promulgating erroneous Christian doctrine
ψευδολόγος.as:
* ψευδο-λόγος, -ον
(< ψευδής, λέγω),
speaking falsely, lying: I Ti 4:2 (Aristoph., Polyb., al.).†

ψευδώνυμος.long: falsely named, under a false name.
ψευδώνυμος.as:
* ψευδώνυμος, -ον
(< ψευδής, ὄνομα)
under a false name, falsely called: I Ti 6:20 (Æsch., Plut., al.).†

ψευδοδιδάσκαλος.long: a false teacher, teacher of false things.
ψευδοδιδάσκαλος.sd: a spurious teacher, i.e. propagator of erroneous Christian doctrine
ψευδοδιδάσκαλος.as:
† ψευδο-διδάσκαλος, -ου, ὁ
a false teacher: II Pe 2:1.†
